title: Lawrence Rountree v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC denied the appeal and sustained Covenant Presbytery's divestiture without censure. The single issue was whether Presbytery erred under BCO 34-10; the SJC held it did not. No censure was imposed, no other relief was granted, and the divestiture remained in effect.
first_summary: A minister appealed Covenant Presbytery's decision to divest him without censure after he remained on its rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years. The SJC denied the appeal, holding that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed Presbytery to proceed because the three-year limit had long passed and he had no call to a particular ministry. The divestiture remained in place.
summary: After a minister remained on his presbytery's rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years, the presbytery completed involuntary divestiture without censure. He appealed. The SJC denied the appeal and sustained the divestiture, reasoning that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed the presbytery to follow that procedure once the constitutional three-year limit had long passed and no call to a particular ministry was available. The action therefore left the divestiture without censure in force.
